review_candidates.description: About the Company Resourced, Inc. is a non-profit organization focused on international development in the food and agriculture sectors. At Resourced, we are on a mission to increase access to more nutritious foods and diverse, productive crops and transform the livelihoods of smallholder farmers and agricultural value-chain entrepreneurs. We do that by identifying, accelerating, and implementing systems-level innovations in food and agriculture. Our approach is one grown from decades of expertise in food production, agriculture development, and business management with a strong belief in the power of interdisciplinary collaboration. Our Vision: To create a world where food is plentiful and nutritionally rich, and agriculture systems nurture both people and planet. Our Mission: We’re on a mission to reimagine and redesign resilient food systems for an abundant future. We do this with a commercial mindset, cutting-edge technology, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Program Overview Marketing for TELA (M4T) is a three-year initiative focused on accelerating farmer adoption of TELA® maize hybrids in Nigeria by building the marketing and commercialization capacity of the seed enterprises that bring it to market. Led by Resourced (RSCD) and building on the evidence base of the Seed Marketing Innovations for Africa (SMIA) program, M4T introduces an enterprise-oriented commercialization platform that complements existing sector awareness, advocacy, and value chain development efforts of other ecosystem partners, and concentrates on the conversion of farmer awareness into sustainable demand creation and seed sales. By strengthening how seed enterprises market and sell, generating farmer demand and sales conversion, reinforcing public trust and market perception, and establishing a replicable model, the program ensures that TELA's proven genetic performance translates into farmer uptake at scale, especially in the priority states of Kaduna, Niger, and Gombe. The approach is digital-first but right-sized to the channels that work locally, grounded in Nigeria-specific market evidence and customer insights, and refined each season through a continuous improvement cycle. The M4T program will deliver an integrated package of marketing support services (MSS) across five core workstreams: Seed Enterprise Development : Develop functional excellence in seed marketing for active TELA seed companies so they can create and sustain demand independently over time. Market Intelligence : Build a rigorous, country-specific understanding of the local market, customer segments, and sales dynamics to ground all program activities on evidence. Positioning & Branding : Develop a differentiated, credible value proposition for TELA and equip seed companies with positioning and messaging needed to sell effectively. Launch & Operationalize : Design and execute digital-first marketing campaigns with local creative agency partners that increase awareness, leads and sales of TELA varieties. TELA Umbrella : Complement ecosystem efforts to reinforce public trust, create public-private alignment and ensure replicability of approach for other countries and products. Resourced serves as program lead and delivery partner, operating the enterprise-oriented commercialization layer focusing on brand-specific marketing, demand creation and replicable platform delivery, while collaborating closely with core ecosystem partners, such as AATF, Maize Alliance (Augmentum), and AgPAC. Nigeria's licensed TELA seed companies participate through a tiered support and co-investment model, with regional and Nigerian creative agencies delivering campaign training, design, and execution. Position Summary Resourced is seeking a Country Program Manager (CPM) to lead implementation of the M4T program in Nigeria. The CPM owns the program's relationships with participating seed enterprises, directs the market intelligence and commercial planning that inform program co-investment strategy, serves as the primary interface with creative agency partners on campaign development and delivery, and manages the Nigeria-based field team. The role combines commercial judgment in seed marketing with the operational discipline to run a multi-partner program across priority states in Nigeria. This is a country lead role – directly managing the country field team as well as interfacing with collaborative ecosystem partners. Building trust and credibility in working relationships will be critical for success. The role will balance big-picture commercial strategy with detailed seasonal work-planning, and leading a team with executing directly. The CPM leads implementation, holds partners to their commitments, and makes the practical calls on sequencing campaign activity against seed availability, seasonal windows, and security conditions. Success is measured by the program's apex indicator: the share of available TELA seed inventory sold by supported companies – achieved by companies investing directly in marketing TELA and a model Resourced can carry into new markets. Key Responsibilities and Deliverables Within approved workplans and budgets, the CPM has authority to manage the country team, sequence activities, convene partners, review agency deliverables, and recommend adjustments to company support and campaign implementation. Material changes to program strategy, company eligibility, contracts, or approved budgets require Program Director (PD) approval. Beyond the country team, the CPM delivers via partners (ex: seedcos and ecosystem partners) over whom RSCD holds no direct authority, where keeping activities aligned to program outcomes depends on influence, credibility, and consistent follow-through. Country Implementation Leadership – Own delivery of the Nigeria workplan across all five MSS workstreams, translating annual plans into seasonal schedules and tracking delivery against milestones. Adjust sequencing where seed supply, regulatory timing, or security conditions require, and partner with the PD on annual planning. Seed Enterprise Engagement and Co-investment – Serve as the primary relationship lead for participating seed companies, running diagnostics, guiding marketing plan development, and negotiating and monitoring co-investment commitments. Hold regular business reviews on campaign performance, leads, sales conversion, inventory, and marketing expenditure. Market Intelligence and Commercial Planning – Lead company, customer, channel, and geographic analysis across the priority markets, and translate that evidence into company support plans, campaign briefs, seasonal priorities, and resource allocation. Maintain current intelligence on company readiness, seed availability, agro-dealer coverage, farmer demand, and barriers to TELA adoption. Creative Agency and Campaign Oversight – Manage the interface with regional and Nigerian creative agency partners, briefing campaigns, reviewing creative and media plans, confirming Hausa localization, and holding delivery to quality, timing, and budget. Guide lead capture and follow-up while ensuring seed companies retain responsibility for customer contact, pricing, and sales conversion. Ecosystem and Sector Coordination – Represent M4T with AATF, Maize Sector Alliance (Augmentum), AgPAC, public agencies, research institutions, and channel actors. Support the Joint Planning Forum and bilateral co-working groups to keep demand creation synchronized with seed availability and messaging consistent across the sector. Team Leadership – Build and manage the Nigeria field team, onboarding and managing the Field Officer(s), Program Coordinator(s), and in-country contractors, setting clear performance objectives and delivering feedback that enables the team to achieve program objectives. Adapt responsibilities as priorities shift across a distributed, largely remote team. Performance and Reporting – Own country results, reporting, and risk management. Administer the country's portion of the Results Framework, oversee MLE and company data quality, produce internal and funder reporting, monitor budget expenditures against approved lines, and maintain the country risk register. Qualifications Bachelor's degree required in agriculture, agribusiness, marketing, business, or a related field. Master's degree preferred. 8-12 years of relevant experience in seed systems (seed sales, marketing and/or operations) agricultural commercialization, agri-input marketing, or agricultural program management in Nigeria. Demonstrated commercial experience with seed companies, agri-input firms, or FMCG distribution. Direct seed sector experience strongly preferred. People management experience, including field-based staff across multiple locations. Experience managing creative agencies, marketers, or campaign delivery preferred. Working knowledge of the Nigerian seed sector, agro-dealer channel, and northern Nigeria maize markets. Strong stakeholder management skills across private sector, public agencies, and donor-funded programs. Proficiency in English and Hausa required. Additional local Nigerian languages are a plus. Willingness to travel frequently within Nigeria, with periodic regional travel. Location Nigeria-based, Abuja preferred. Regular travel to priority states (Kaduna, Niger, Gombe) and partner sites. Occasional regional travel for trainings, convenings, or stakeholder exchanges Position Type Independent contractor (full-time); annual contract, renewable Start Date November 1, 2026 Pay range and compensation package Compensation is commensurate with education and experience.
